newsitem.title: KENYA: Exile group says Rwandan refugees face starvation.
newsitem.headline: Exile group says Rwandan refugees face starvation.

text.p: A Rwandan exile group said on Sunday that hundreds of thousands of Rwandan refugees in Zaire and Tanzania faced starvation.
The Union for the Return of Refugees and Democracy to Rwanda (RDR), a mainly Hutu group with headquarters in Belgium, said in a statement faxed to Reuters: "The refugee crisis is far from resolved."
The RDR said more than half a million Rwandans remained in eastern Zaire between Walikali and Kisangani -- an area which is not controlled by rebels who have seized large areas further east.

"In Zaire there are more than 500,000 refugees in the geographical zone between Walikali and Kisangani who are in danger of a certain death if the international community does not quickly come to their aid," it said.
U.N. officials in Rwanda said the figures for the number of regugees quoted by the RDR were too high.
According to the U.N. refugee agency UNHCR, 1.2 million Rwandan refugees have returned to Rwanda from Zaire and Tanzania since last November.
UNHCR figures say 719,307 Rwandans returned home from eastern Zaire last year, and more than 480,000 returned from Tanzania during December.
The UNHCR said more than 350,000 Rwandans were still stranded in eastern Zaire earlier this month.
The Tanzanian government says "only small concentrations" of Rwandans now remain in Tanzania.

The massive return home by Hutus who fled Rwanda after the 1994 genocide of some 800,000 Tutsis and others was prompted by a Tutsi-led uprising in eastern Zaire which began in October. Tanzania then put pressure on the Rwandan refugees on its soil to join the exodus.
